covers.title: The Red Cup
covers.scene: A cosy Japanese kitchen in morning sunlight. An eight-year-old Japanese girl with a dark bob and a yellow cardigan has just set a small bright red ceramic cup on a wooden breakfast table beside a white plate. A curious ginger-and-white cat sits near the table looking towards the cup. The girl's hand still rests beside it; an ordinary domestic moment with a hint that the cat has plans. Focus on the red cup, child and cat. Soft cream, honey and red palette.

covers.title: The Ticket in the Pocket

She is searching one coat pocket with a mildly puzzled smile while he holds a blue cloth shopping bag open to help. Platform roof, a bench and a waiting local train softly behind them. A gingko leaf lies on the bench; quiet affectionate humour. Do not show a found ticket, no readable signs or numbers.

covers.title: The Tiny Cinema
covers.scene: A Japanese family's living room on a rainy afternoon during a power cut. A boy aged eleven in a blue sweatshirt kneels on a rug, holding up an ordinary camping torch towards a blank pale sheet hung safely across a doorway. A folded-paper rabbit and simple cardboard shapes lie on the low table beside him. His mother in a coral cardigan sits nearby, intrigued. Show the preparations for an improvised shadow theatre, before the show. Rain streaks on a window, soft torch glow, indigo and warm amber. No projected movie, no electronics switched on.

covers.title: Fireworks Without Sound
covers.scene: A quiet Japanese riverside before a summer fireworks festival, at deep blue dusk. A fourteen-year-old Japanese girl in an indigo summer yukata with tiny white dots walks beside her grandfather, a gentle elderly man in a light linen shirt who wears small hearing aids. They stop beside a still irrigation canal reflecting the last pink light. Festival lights are distant on the far riverbank; foreground reeds, a folded pale blue picnic cloth under her arm. They are looking for their viewing place. Anticipation, intimate and luminous. No fireworks yet, no outcome spoilers.

covers.title: The Photo Studio After Closing
covers.scene: Inside a small old Japanese portrait photography studio after sunset. A Japanese woman photographer in her thirties with a chin-length dark haircut and a moss-green work apron stands beside a wooden counter, carefully examining a faded photograph offered by an elderly Japanese man in a navy cardigan. The photo faces away from the viewer. An old camera, softbox, framed portraits turned indistinct and a darkroom curtain create a layered workspace. A desk lamp makes a pool of amber light against cool blue windows. Quietly compelling, emotionally restrained, no readable text.

covers.title: Tomorrow’s Lost Property
covers.scene: A quietly uncanny municipal lost-property office in Japan just before opening, rainy grey light outside. A Japanese woman clerk in her early thirties with short black hair and a simple muted burgundy cardigan stands at a long desk examining a small cobalt-blue child's mitten in a clear shallow tray. Beside it is a plain paper tag with absolutely no writing visible, and a tall metal shelving unit holds a few umbrellas and ordinary objects. Across the window the city wakes under rain. A wall clock has an indistinct unlettered face. Literary speculative fiction, restrained magic, slate, burgundy and luminous cobalt palette. Only one clerk, one mitten, no floating objects or visual special effects.
